results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a first-order language and $f : \alpha \to \beta$ a map. results.title: Unfolding the definition of a p-ordering
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. results.title: Building a p-ordering
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. If $S$ is infinite, $a_n \in S$ for every $n$, and $v_n(a_n) \le v_n(x)$ for every $n$ and every $x \in S$, then $(a_n)$ is a $\mathfrak p$-ordering of $S$.

results.title: The stage-zero valuation vanishes

results.title: The stage-zero condition of a p-ordering is automatic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a Dedekind domain, $\mathfrak p$ a nonzero prime ideal of $R$, $S \subseteq R$ and $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ a sequence in $R$, and write $v_n$ for the stage-$n$ prefix-product valuation with respect to $\mathfrak p$ and $(a_n)$. results.title: Rectilinear cycle
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A rectilinear cycle is a finitely supported function from rectilinear rectangles to $\mathbb{Z}$, that is, a finite formal sum $\sum_r n_r\, r$ of rectilinear rectangles $r$ with integer coefficients $n_r$, read as the corresponding integer combination of oriented rectangle boundaries.

results.title: The cycle of a single rectangle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a rectilinear rectangle $r$, this is the rectilinear cycle in which $r$ has coefficient $1$ and every other rectangle has coefficient $0$, that is, the boundary of $r$ with the orientation given by its corner order.

results.title: Contour integral over a rectilinear cycle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a complex Banach space and $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$. For a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$, a finite formal sum $\sum_r n_r\, r$ of rectangles $r$ with integer coefficients $n_r$, the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ is $\sum_r n_r \int_{\partial r} f$, where $\int_{\partial r} f$ is the boundary integral of $f$ over the oriented rectangle $r$.

results.title: Additivity of the contour integral in the cycle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a complex Banach space and $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$. For rectilinear cycles $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$, the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma + \Lambda$ equals the integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ plus the integral of $f$ over $\Lambda$.

results.title: Reversing a cycle negates its integral
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$, every complex Banach space $E$ and every function $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$, the contour integral of $f$ over $-\Gamma$ is the negative of the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$.

results.title: Integral over a difference of cycles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For rectilinear cycles $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$, a complex Banach space $E$ and a function $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$, the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma - \Lambda$ equals the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ minus the contour integral of $f$ over $\Lambda$.

results.title: Contour integration as an additive map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $E$ be a complex Banach space and $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$. The map sending a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$ to the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ is an additive group homomorphism from rectilinear cycles to $E$.

results.title: Rectangle filling supported in a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. A rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$, read as a filling by rectangles, is supported in $G$ when, for every rectangle $r$ whose coefficient in $\Gamma$ is nonzero, the closed carrier of $r$ is contained in $G$.

results.title: Cauchy–Goursat theorem for rectilinear cycles
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a complex Banach space, let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, and let $f : \mathbb{C} \to E$ be complex differentiable on $G$. If $\Gamma$ is a rectilinear cycle whose rectangle filling is supported in $G$, that is, the closed rectangle of every rectangle occurring in $\Gamma$ with nonzero coefficient is contained in $G$, then the contour integral of $f$ over $\Gamma$ is $0$.

results.title: Rectilinear cycles homologous in a set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G \subseteq \mathbb{C}$. Two rectilinear cycles $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are homologous in $G$ when the rectangle filling of $\Gamma - \Lambda$ is supported in $G$: every rectangle with nonzero coefficient in $\Gamma - \Lambda$ has its closed carrier contained in $G$.

results.title: Index of a rectilinear cycle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$ and a point $w \in \mathbb{C}$, the index of $\Gamma$ about $w$ is $\frac{1}{2\pi i}\int_\Gamma \frac{dz}{z - w}$, the contour integral over $\Gamma$ of $z \mapsto (z - w)^{-1}$, multiplied by $(2\pi i)^{-1}$.

results.title: Winding index as an additive map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a fixed point $w \in \mathbb{C}$, the map sending a rectilinear cycle $\Gamma$ to its index about $w$ is an additive group homomorphism from rectilinear cycles to $\mathbb{C}$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an axis-parallel rectangle $r$ and a point $w \in \mathbb{C}$ outside the closed carrier of $r$, the index about $w$ of the cycle consisting of the boundary of $r$ is $0$.

results.title: Partition of an interval
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For real numbers $a$ and $b$, a partition of the closed interval $[a, b]$ consists of a natural number $n$, the number of subintervals, together with $n + 1$ points forming a strictly increasing sequence $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$.

results.title: Tagged partition
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A tagged partition of $[a, b]$ is a partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ together with a choice of a tag $\xi_k \in [x_{k-1}, x_k]$ in each subinterval, for $k = 1, \dots, n$.

results.title: Mesh of a partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mesh (also called the norm) of a partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ is the maximum subinterval length $\max_{1 \le k \le n} (x_k - x_{k-1})$ when $n \ge 1$, and $0$ when $n = 0$.

results.title: Points of a partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The point set of a partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ is the set of its points $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_n$.

results.title: Refinement of a partition
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For partitions $P$ and $Q$ of $[a, b]$, $Q$ is a refinement of $P$ when every point of $P$ is a point of $Q$, that is, when the point set of $P$ is contained in the point set of $Q$.

results.title: Riemann sum
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $T$ be a tagged partition of $[a, b]$, with points $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ and tags $\xi_k \in [x_{k-1}, x_k]$ for $k = 1, \dots, n$. The Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $T$ is $S_f(x, \xi) = \sum_{k=1}^{n} f(\xi_k)\,(x_k - x_{k-1})$ (an empty sum, equal to $0$, when $n = 0$).

results.title: Endpoints of a partition are ordered
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ and the interval $[a, b]$ has a partition, then $a \le b$.

results.title: A partition of a nondegenerate interval has a subinterval
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $a < b$, then every partition $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ of $[a, b]$ has at least one subinterval, that is, $n \ge 1$.

results.title: The mesh is positive on a nondegenerate interval

results.title: Riemann sum over a trivial partition
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and every tagged partition of $[a, b]$ with no subintervals, the Riemann sum of $f$ is $0$, since it is an empty sum.

results.title: Subintervals of a partition have nonnegative length
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ is a partition of $[a, b]$, then $x_{i+1} - x_i \ge 0$ for every $i$ with $0 \le i < n$.

results.title: Subinterval lengths are at most the mesh
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $a = x_0 < x_1 < \dots < x_n = b$ be a partition of $[a, b]$. Then for every $i$ with $0 \le i < n$, the subinterval length $x_{i+1} - x_i$ is at most the mesh of the partition.

results.title: Subinterval lengths of a partition telescope
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $a = x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n = b$ is a partition of $[a, b]$, then the lengths of its subintervals sum to the length of the interval: $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (x_{i+1} - x_i) = b - a$.
